project.title: Bioelectrochemical Sulfur Autotrophic Denitrification with Sulfur-Based Cathodes  Enhanced Nitrogen Removal and Mechanism
project.description: Traditional Sulfur Autotrophic Denitrification (SAD) technology faces low nitrogen removal efficiency owing to subpar electron transfer and inadequate microbial cooperation. It also tends to accumulate nitrites, driving up operational costs. Integrating a bioelectrochemical system (BES) with SAD creates a highly efficient and sustainable solution for controlling nitrogen pollution. This study presents the development of innovative sulfur-based cathode electrode materials and the construction of an enhanced bioelectrochemical sulfur autotrophic denitrification system. Compared to conventional BES and SAD, BESAD showed higher nitrogen removal efficiency. At 0.7 , its nitrate removal rate was 99.32, with a nitrogen removal load of 0.37 . Applied voltage accelerated nitrate removal, improving electron transfer and microbial activity. Microbial community richness and evenness increased with voltage, particularly for functional microbes like Pseudomonas. In BESAD, the extracellular polymer concentration and PN/PS ratio increased with voltage, thereby enhancing microbial metabolism and improving biofilm structure. Dissolved organic matter (DOM) analysis revealed that electrochemical drive promoted the formation of simple aromatic proteins and soluble microbial products, reflecting voltage-induced metabolic shifts. Voltage-regulation BESAD with sulfur cathodes enhances nitrogen removal, electron transfer, and the proliferation of functional microbes, outperforming traditional SAD. This study offers key insights for developing bioelectrochemical sulfur autotrophic denitrification technology.
